metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art run — the dispatcher case at art:99-101 that wraps `bash runtime/scripts/run.sh`. run.sh is the ONE command that gates paperwork (F), lints the beat mix (L), enforces finance chart-shape (SHAPE), pre-flights static scenes (A) and WCAG margins (W), renders each pending Manim scene with layout audit (B), fills every Remotion beat via runtime/scripts/remotion_scenes.py, compiles a review cut via compile.py --review, and closes with frame-level visual QC (V) on the finished mp4. It writes <slug>-slate.mp4 (the review cut) and skips slots already filled. Not a final master — `./art final` is the separate verb. Aliases: none; dispatcher matches only 'run'. Env knobs: ART_QC=0 (skip gates), ART_STRICT=0 (warnings not blockers), ART_FACTS=0 (previz exception on Gate F), --height (default 2160). All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workspace against a fixture reel at /tmp/claude-501/art-run-demo. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. No paid API, no upload, no network calls. episode.source_sha256 f9c007cae04ca87ddb005388bf8c0835e220369e6f2d2377dd54f02e1f6c65c2.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the gate order run.sh actually runs.
beats.narration_text: Here is the loop the script actually runs, in order. Gate F — the paperwork triad: FACTCHECK, SHOTLIST, PROMPTS. Gate L — beat-mix lint: no single-sentence text slides. Gate SHAPE — finance chart-shape enforcement, if this is a finance reel. Gate A — static pre-flight on every pending Manim scene. Gate W — WCAG contrast and margins on the same scenes. Then it renders each pending Manim scene and runs Gate B — layout audit — on it before slotting. Then it fills every Remotion beat. Then it compiles a slate cut. Then Gate V — frame-level visual QC on the finished mp4. Any gate can stop the build.

props.title: run.sh — the loop, in order
props.code:
# runtime/scripts/run.sh — one command, ten stages.
#
# Gate F  — paperwork triad present   (FACTCHECK · SHOTLIST · PROMPTS)
# Gate L  — beat-mix lint              (no single-sentence text slides)
# Gate SHAPE — finance chart-shape     (sankey/mirrored-bar/… — finance only)
# Gate A  — static pre-flight          (per pending Manim scene, no render)
# Gate W  — WCAG contrast + margins    (same scenes, independent 2nd check)
#   for each pending Manim scene:
#     manim -qk --fps 24 -r $RES scenes.py $Scene
# Gate B  — layout audit (rendered PNG) (per scene, before slotting)
#     mv $out $REEL/manim/$BID.mp4
# runtime/scripts/remotion_scenes.py $REEL      # fill every Remotion beat
# runtime/scripts/compile.py $REEL --review     # review cut with markers
# Gate V  — frame-level visual QC on the finished mp4
#
# ANY gate can stop the build. ART_QC=0 skips them all.
props.sparkLine: Ten stages. Any one of them can stop it.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — art run vs art final; two verbs, two files.
beats.narration_text: Two verbs, two files on disk. Art run writes slug dash slate dot mp4 — the review cut with beat markers burned in. Art final writes slug dot mp4 — the clean master, only after every gate passes and after the compiler's atomic verification stamps a receipt beside it. If you see a slate label on your export, you ran the wrong verb. Both commands compile the same beats — the difference is what gets stamped on top and whether the receipt is written.

props.title: run vs final — two verbs, two files
props.code:
$ ./art run   <reel>            # REVIEW cut
  -> writes <reel>/<slug>-slate.mp4     (beat markers on top)
  -> runs Gate F/L/SHAPE/A/W/B, then compile.py --review,
     then Gate V frame-check on the finished mp4.
  -> no verified receipt; iterate freely.

# --------------------------- vs -----------------------------

$ ./art final <reel>            # MASTER cut  (default --height 2160)
  -> writes <reel>/<slug>.mp4            (clean, no markers)
  -> runs the same gates + compile.py's atomic verification
     (verified.json beside the mp4, sha-256 + input digests).
  -> build-state.json status = "ready" on success.

# The compiler's mandatory verification is the difference:
# a slate cut is a preview; a final cut is a receipt.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code from your reel folder. Run art run once. Read the last four lines. If a gate is the failure, the message names which one and how to unblock. If Remotion is the failure, read the beat id it printed and re-run that beat's audio and scene alone. Then re-run art run — it will skip every filled slot. The loop should shorten by one on every pass. If it does not, a slot is not being written, and the message names which one.
